manifest.name: dsh-anthropic-image-clamp
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness host plugin: downscale inline images on Anthropic Messages requests so many-image requests never exceed the 2000px per-side limit.
manifest.author: Noah Chalifour

bundle.text:
# dsh-anthropic-image-clamp — bundle self-activation patch.
# Override in the profile's cordis.patch.yml, e.g.:
#   - id: anthropic-image-clamp
#     config: { maxDimension: 1568 }
- insert:
    - id: anthropic-image-clamp
      name: dsh-anthropic-image-clamp
      config:
        maxDimension: 2000
        hosts: [api.anthropic.com]

readme.text:
Stops this Claude error in DeepSeek Harness:

```
messages.N.content.M.image.source.base64.data: At least one of the image
dimensions exceed max allowed size for many-image requests: 2000 pixels
```

**Cause.** Anthropic allows up to 8000px per side, but a request carrying
more than 20 images is capped at 2000px per side. DSH normalizes attachments
to a 2048×2048 *pixel budget* (8192px long edge), so a phone screenshot such as
1080×2400 is stored as-is. Once a session's history holds more than 20 images,
every request fails.

**Fix.** This host plugin wraps `fetch` for `api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`
requests and downscales any inline base64 image whose longer side exceeds
`maxDimension` (default 2000). The results are deterministic and cached by
content hash, so re-sent history stays byte-identical and the prompt cache
still hits.

Install, then restart DSH:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:noahchalifour/dsh-anthropic-image-clamp
```

Config override (profile `cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: anthropic-image-clamp
  config: { maxDimension: 1568, hosts: [api.anthropic.com] }
```

Limitation: requests routed through a subscriptions-plugin HTTP proxy use
undici's own fetch and bypass the wrapper. No proxy is configured on this
machine.
